sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a two-arm trial; the probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\) are known protocol-fixed design inputs and are not conditions defining either compatible-law class.
sampling_model.units: Each unit has finite genomic profile \(Z\), a predeclared continuous score \(R\), bounded potential event times, and potential censoring times.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) is independent of \((T(0),T(1),C(0),C(1))\) conditional on \(X=(Z,R)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The lower bounds \(\pi_a(x)\ge\varepsilon\) hold for both treatment arms, and uncensored probability is bounded below by \(\kappa\). Because treatment is binary and the two allocation probabilities sum to one, \(\pi_a(x)\le1-\varepsilon\) is a consequence rather than a separate overlap restriction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The bounded score-density and known-\(\beta\) Hölder conditions are explicit maintained regularity restrictions. No nuisance-band theorem is inferred from them. Inference is stated only over the externally certified subclass \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\), with abstract radius \(r_n\), and the empirical-process prerequisite is imposed only on \(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.1 bounds each covariatewise CATE by differencing armwise conservative CAPO endpoints.
The paper characterizes sharp response-function regions under selective observation and shape restrictions using random-set capacity and Aumann-expectation methods.
Theorem 1 gives sharp DTE bounds under support restrictions by optimal-transport duality.
Theorem 1 computes projections of a shape-restricted sieve confidence region by two linear programs.
Theorems 3.2 and 4.1 derive directional limits for uniform functionals of optimized value maps with a fixed feasible correspondence.
The paper diagnoses ordinary-bootstrap failure for nonlinear directional derivatives and validates derivative-aware resampling.
Theorem 3.1 gives a uniform Gaussian support-function process for set-identified linear models using orthogonal moments and sample splitting.
Theorem 1 gives efficient joint Gaussian inference for a supplied family of point-identified subgroup effects.
The paper constructs winner's-curse-adjusted inference for a selected approximately Gaussian scalar target.

body.tldr: Informative dropout leaves an unknown residual survival contribution at every prognostic-score value. Two novel identifying restrictions, nondecrease after orienting the score toward better prognosis and a clinically calibrated Lipschitz bound, couple those contributions, so differencing pointwise arm bounds is not a joint identified set. The proposal characterizes the exact compact convex CATE-curve set, proves attainability even where dropout capacity is zero, separates every support direction into arm-profile obstacle problems, certifies each grid problem by a path min-cost-flow dual, and gives a uniform Hausdorff discretization bound. A separate residual-continuity-only compatible-law class has the Wang endpoint box as its exact identified image, while an observed score-pair criterion is sufficient for strict contraction. Inference is posed only on an externally certified band-valid subclass at abstract radius \(r_n\); a finite \(\delta_n\)-net of gridded support directions yields an explicit \(2\mathsf R\delta_n\) Hausdorff remainder and a \(\log|\mathcal D_n|\) calibration cost. Conditional on those band and finite-net empirical-process prerequisites, the open kernel asks for derivative-aware whole-set and finite-VC leaf coverage as contacts change; arbitrary selected-leaf inclusion is a corollary.

project_justification.gap: Wang et al. identify only covariatewise endpoint bounds and report adaptively favorable ADJUVANT leaves. Random-set, shape-restricted, optimized-value, and subgroup-inference papers each supply one ingredient but do not solve joint curve sharpness with estimated dropout obstacles or prove attainability of the continuous endpoint image as a distinct compatible-law class.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a law-sharp function-valued region whose capacity can vanish, whose numerical representation has a checkable certificate, and whose support map is nonsmooth because its feasible correspondence is estimated.
project_justification.fill: Separate completion lemmas settle identification for the maintained monotone-Lipschitz class and the residual-continuity-only Wang benchmark; the support and eroded-grid theorems settle computation and approximation. On the externally certified subclass \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\), the open critical-cone construction targets uniform whole-set and finite-VC leaf coverage with the uncompressed external-band, direction-net, and sampling errors displayed separately; post-selection inclusion is only a corollary.

body.related_work: Wang et al. (2025, Theorem 5.1, equations (8)--(9), and Appendix D.2) motivate the clinical problem and supply conservative covariatewise endpoints. The separately defined class \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) retains only residual continuity and has their continuous endpoint image \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) exactly; the maintained monotone-Lipschitz class is distinct and contracts that image strictly under the stated sufficient score-pair condition. The full randomized-design condition, residual restrictions, bounded score density, and known-\(\beta\) Hölder regularity are maintained conditions here, not assumptions attributed to Wang et al. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011, Theorem 2.1 and its support-dominance proof) and their 2012 selective-observation paper inform the measurable-selection and support-function architecture but neither establish the clinical restrictions nor derive either informative-censoring completion. Kim (2014, Theorem 1 and Appendix A) informs the use of primal attainability and dual certificates, while the finite problem here is a path obstacle transshipment rather than a fixed-marginal transport coupling. Chiang et al. (2021, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.1) inform how continuous shape constraints become linear inequalities; they neither establish the present score-density or Hölder conditions nor validate monotonicity or a value of \(L\) in this survival application, and they do not control Hausdorff distance between identified sets. Westling et al. (2024, Theorems 1--3) inform cross-fitted uniform survival signals under identifying censoring assumptions. Semenova (2023, Theorem 3.1) informs orthogonal support-boundary estimation for finite-dimensional set-linear models. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Theorems 3.2 and 4.1) and Fang and Santos (2019, Sections 2--3) inform directional inference for nonsmooth optimized maps, but contain no result for an estimated obstacle correspondence with changing zero-capacity contacts. Wei et al. (2023, Theorem 1) inform joint inference for prespecified point-identified subgroups, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2024) inform selected-scalar inference; the open coverage construction instead takes an externally certified nuisance band on \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\) and score-process controls only on the finite index \(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\) as explicit prerequisites and calibrates the whole curve set and every eligible leaf in one supremum, with selected-leaf inclusion only as its immediate corollary. Liu et al. (2021) supply the ADJUVANT genomic destination and the small-cell motivation, not an econometric comparator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The completion uses the convention \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{C\le T\}\), so assigning \(T=C\) to the non-maximal branch remains recorded as dropout. If a data system codes ties as observed events, exact attainment at zero residual may fail and the sharp object can become a closure; that alternative convention must be audited before application.
body.honest_scope: The law-sharpness, support-flow, grid-Hausdorff, residual-continuity benchmark, and sufficient strict-contraction claims are theorem targets. Known allocation probabilities are protocol-fixed design inputs. Lower overlap for both binary arms implies the corresponding upper bound, which is not imposed separately. The bounded score-density and observed-law Hölder conditions are explicit regularity restrictions; \(\beta\in(0,1]\) is known and fixed before inference. Residual monotonicity and the finite-\(L\) restriction are novel identifying sensitivities with the stated external validation and clinical calibration protocol. No honest nuisance band or rate is claimed to follow from this model. All inferential claims are uniform only over the externally certified subclass \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\). The empirical-process prerequisite is restricted to the finite direction net \(\mathcal D_n\) and eligible leaves, and the uncompressed error retains \(r_n/p_{\min,n}\), \(\mathsf R\delta_n\), and the sampling term with \(\log|\mathcal D_n|\). An \(O_P(r_n)\) whole-set rate is asserted only under the displayed balancing conditions. The changing-contact coverage construction remains open; selected-leaf inclusion is only a corollary. The ADJUVANT reanalysis requires trial records, a predeclared score, and an eligible leaf; if every honest sign interval contains zero, the conclusion is non-robust.
